title: Ezekiel Bible Quiz - Chapter 31
description: Ten questions on Ezekiel 31: the cedar in Lebanon told to Pharaoh, the tree the nations lived under, and its fall to the lower parts of the earth.

questions.text: To whom was the prophet told to tell this message about greatness?
questions.explanation: He was told to say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and his multitude: Whom are you like in your greatness?

questions.text: What is the Assyrian compared to in this chapter?
questions.explanation: It says: behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with beautiful branches, with a forest-like shade and of high stature.

answers.text: To a lion in the field
To a monster in the seas
To a tower on a hill

questions.text: What made the tree grow, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: It says the waters nourished it, the deep made it grow, and its rivers ran all around its plantation.

questions.text: What did the birds of the sky do in the tree's boughs?
questions.explanation: It says all the birds of the sky made their nests in its boughs, and that under its branches all the animals of the field gave birth to their young.

questions.text: What does the chapter say about the trees in the garden of God?
questions.explanation: It says the cedars in the garden of God could not hide it, the cypress trees were not like its boughs, and no tree in the garden of God was like it in beauty.

answers.text: No tree there was like it in beauty
They were cut down before it

questions.text: How did all the trees of Eden feel about this tree?
questions.explanation: It says: I made it beautiful by the multitude of its branches, so that all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied it.

questions.text: Into whose hand would the tree be delivered because its heart was lifted up?
questions.explanation: Because he was exalted in stature and his heart was lifted up in his height, he would be delivered into the hand of the mighty one of the nations.

answers.text: Into the hand of the mighty one of the nations
Into the hand of the birds of the sky
Into the hand of the trees of Eden
Into the hand of the shepherds of the land

questions.text: Who cut the tree off and left it?
questions.explanation: It says strangers, the tyrants of the nations, have cut him off and have left him, and that his branches have fallen on the mountains and in the valleys.

answers.text: The animals of the field and the valleys
The princes of the sea and the islands
Strangers, the tyrants of the nations
The waters of the deep and the rivers

questions.text: What was caused to happen in the day the tree went down to Sheol?
questions.explanation: It says that in the day he went down to Sheol he caused a mourning, covered the deep for him, and caused Lebanon to mourn for him.

answers.text: The rivers were made to overflow
The trees of Eden were planted again
The birds returned to its boughs
Lebanon was caused to mourn for him

questions.text: Whom does the end of the chapter say this tree is?
questions.explanation: The chapter closes by saying: this is Pharaoh and all his multitude, says the Lord Yahweh.
